extracted.intended_audience: readers and students of early‑modern maritime exploration, commanders, and historians
extracted.subtask_description: Prescriptive and practical guidance embedded in an early‑modern voyage narrative about command decisions, seamanship, provisioning, discipline, treatment of natives, and crisis management on long oceanic expeditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear orders from sovereigns/commanders
rubrics_metrics.description: Sovereigns, he said, when they undertake great enterprises, ought to distinguish, make clear, and strengthen their orders in such a way that the persons to whom their execution is entrusted can have no room for doubt, nor to contend, nor any one who can make excuses
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not pledge men so that they find themselves in confused and difficult positions; issue unambiguous directives so subordinates cannot reasonably dispute, excuse, or misinterpret them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plan realistic voyage duration
rubrics_metrics.description: To make such a grand voyage as this twenty months are enough, or at the outside two years
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate total voyage time conservatively based on known routes and seasons; recognise multi‑voyage projects may require many expeditions to complete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider seasonal winds and weather in route decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: he knew... there was the beginning of those furious westerlies which last at least until the first days of October, for which cause it was impossible to go there at that season
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attempting certain routes at seasons known for adverse prevailing winds; select timing and course to minimize exposure to known seasonal storms or headwinds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure adequate and safe provisioning (water and food)
rubrics_metrics.description: there was very little water left and no meat: for the Chief Pilot had buried the casks among the ballast where the bilge‑water sucked in, and for that reason it had all turned bad
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Store water and provisions where they cannot be contaminated by bilge or spoilage; keep reserves, and monitor stores to avoid critical shortages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include medical personnel and comforts for the sick
rubrics_metrics.description: He felt that he had many sick, and no medical man, nor the necessary comforts to nourish them
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voyages should carry medical attendants and suitable provisions/comforts for ill crew to reduce mortality and maintain morale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rely on competent pilots and trustworthy crew
rubrics_metrics.description: it might with truth be said that he was without pilots on whom he could rely, and that from some other persons there was little to be expected or hoped
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select and trust only skilled, dependable navigators and officers; the absence of reliable pilots undermines decision‑making in danger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use natural signs for navigation and to judge proximity to land
rubrics_metrics.description: the Captain, knowing by that weed, and many others of the same kind, that the land was near, ordered an E.S.E. course to be steered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Observe seaweed, birds, seals, and floating timber as indicators of nearby land; change course accordingly rather than relying solely on instruments in uncertain conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain continuous, disciplined lookouts
rubrics_metrics.description: Much care was exercised with regard to the look‑outs. At night there were two men on the bowsprit, and in the daytime one at each masthead
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deploy multiple lookouts by time of day/position to detect hazards or land early; formalise shifts and positions to ensure coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect and conserve rainwater proactively
rubrics_metrics.description: With twenty‑eight sheets stretched all over the ship, we collected, from this and another rainfall, three hundred jars of water
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use sails/sheets and containers to harvest rainfall when available; systematic collection can materially relieve water shortages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Base routing decisions on combined factors and choose the least harmful option
rubrics_metrics.description: the best service he could do to His Majesty at present was to save the ship, save time, save the expenses... he ordered the Pilots to shape a course for New Spain and the port of Acapulco
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When faced with competing aims (discovery vs survival vs reporting), prioritise preserving the ship, crew, and ability to report discoveries—choose the 'least of two evils.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Assert command and enforce orders when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: the Captain issued an order to go at once to that port, on pain of grave penalties, because so it was ordered
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A captain must exercise clear authority and threaten or apply penalties to enforce vital commands when subordinates are lukewarm or obstructive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reward merit and sacrifice
rubrics_metrics.description: he who suffered most and should be most useful, would be most worthy of reward
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognise and reward those who endure the greatest hardship and provide most service; use rewards to encourage useful behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Favor measured clemency and avoid summary capital punishment
rubrics_metrics.description: he was determined never to take life or reputation... To pardon ingrates and enemies... was a very great vengeance; and greater courage was shown by having power and not using it
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer piety and forbearance over cruel punishments; exercise justice through proper channels rather than impulsive retaliation; avoid irreversible penalties when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave legal/punitive judgments to appropriate authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: justice was an excellent virtue, and very necessary in the world; but yet let it be exercised by others who have the habit, rather than by him
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A ship's commander should avoid acting as full judicial authority in complex disputes—defer to proper tribunals or those experienced in administering justice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect natives from exploitation and oppose avarice
rubrics_metrics.description: I should not wish... that among these new and tender people there should come to settle... any falcons, or sakers, or other birds of prey... To give a relish to dishes of such impious wickedness... they require from them always more
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advocate fair treatment and prosperity for indigenous peoples; resist and sanction those who pillage, extort, or exploit for money.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide restitution and accountability for abuses
rubrics_metrics.description: they do not return that which they have taken by force, but rather seek anew and with increased eagerness
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep records of injustices and press for restitution; impose penalties and oversight to discourage repeated abuses by colonists or agents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emergency seamanship measures: pumps, scuppers, lighten, cut rigging/masts
rubrics_metrics.description: With water up to their waists, the men succeeded with bars and levers in tearing away some of the planks, so as to allow the water to escape... 'Cut away the main mast; it is that which is taking us to the bottom.' ... they were cutting away the weather rigging
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In severe storms prioritise dewatering (create scuppers), use pumps, jettison weight, and cut masts/rigging as last‑resort measures to regain stability and buoyancy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perform sacraments and religious duties when circumstances demand
rubrics_metrics.description: He ordered the two natives to be brought... the Franciscan Father to ask them whether they wished to be Christians... he baptized them, calling them Pedro and Pablo
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend to the spiritual welfare of converts and those facing mortal danger; commanders often saw conversion/baptism as part of mission duties in critical moments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contingency planning: anchor, build launch, and reassess upon finding land
rubrics_metrics.description: if in the southern part where we were any islands should be found, we were to anchor there to build a launch and come to a new resolution
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include plans for using discovered islands (anchor, repair, gather info, launch boats) and re‑evaluate objectives in light of new opportunities or hazards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitor crew morale and watch for signs of desertion or irrational acts
rubrics_metrics.description: It was conjectured that with a board... he had made a raft, and that he went away on it... He had a strong wish to remain with the natives... This was the act of a man whom we held to be rational
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be alert to individual crew members' mental state, clandestine preparations for desertion, or religious/romantic impulses that could endanger them; investigate and counsel where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record navigational data daily and report discoveries
rubrics_metrics.description: he ordered the Pilots to shape a course... and to give an account of the route they followed, and the latitude each day
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep daily log of course and latitude and ensure accurate reports of discoveries are preserved and transmitted to authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use fishing and local resources to supplement provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain albacore and bonito, in a large shoal... 2,500 arrobas of fish supplied the place of meat, and lasted until we reached the port of Acapulco
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exploit available fisheries and natural resources to stretch provisions; salt and preserve catches for long passages.
